chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Muhammad al-Hajjaj, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is appropriate for the Imam to make audible to those behind him whatever he says, and it is not appropriate for those behind the Imam to make audible to him anything of what he says.

key_terms.يَنْبَغِي: It is appropriate / it is fitting
key_terms.يُسْمِعَ: To make audible / to cause to hear

ai.seo_question: What is the proper auditory etiquette between the Imam and the followers during prayer recitation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the acoustic etiquette of congregational prayer, emphasizing the Imam’s role as the audible leader whose recitation guides the congregation. It establishes a hierarchical auditory dynamic where the Imam’s voice carries forward while the followers’ silence maintains the structural integrity of the collective worship, reflecting the Shia emphasis on order and following the designated leader.
